data:
Subjective
Client reported that they applied for the team lead role, with the interview scheduled for next Friday. Client stated they are already rehearsing what could go wrong and expressed fears that interviewers will realize they are a "fraud" and that they might lose their current job as well.

Objective
Client appeared engaged in the session and was cooperative with the Therapist's interventions. Speech was clear and coherent. Affect was anxious initially when discussing fears related to the upcoming interview, but shifted to more relaxed and insightful during cognitive restructuring and the mock interview. Thought process was logical and goal-directed. Objective measure scores were not assessed this session.

Assessment
Client demonstrated progress toward treatment goals by examining evidence for and against negative self-referent thoughts related to imposter fears. Client was able to recognize that not knowing every answer in meetings does not equate to being a fraud. Diagnostic impressions and risk level were not formally reassessed this session, though client showed a positive response to cognitive restructuring and behavioral rehearsal.

Plan
Continue cognitive restructuring regarding imposter fears and interview anxiety Practice answering difficult interview questions in preparation for next Friday Schedule next individual session for 50 minutes

Presentation
The client presented to the individual session engaged and cooperative. Mood and affect were anxious regarding an upcoming interview. Notable changes since last session include the client submitting an application for the team lead role.

Session content
The main theme discussed was career advancement and associated anxiety. The client reported anticipatory anxiety regarding an upcoming interview next Friday, stating, "I'm already rehearsing what could go wrong." The client expressed fears of being perceived as a fraud, noting, "That they'll realise I'm a fraud and I'll lose the job I have now too."

Interventions
Examined evidence for and against automatic negative thoughts using Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT). Conducted a behavioral experiment through a short mock interview to test anxiety predictions.

Client response
The client actively participated in examining the evidence for the belief that they are a fraud, acknowledging that not knowing every answer in meetings does not equate to being a fraud and noting that their manager also lacks all answers. The client responded well to the mock interview, reporting afterwards, "That was less bad than I expected," indicating a reduction in anticipatory anxiety and increased insight.

Risk assessment
No risk indicators were reported.

Plan
Continue preparing for the upcoming team lead interview. Focus on managing anticipatory anxiety and negative self-talk in the next session. Schedule next appointment.

Behavior
Client presented for a 50-minute individual session, reporting anticipatory anxiety regarding an upcoming interview for a team lead role next Friday. Client reported engaging in anticipatory worry and catastrophizing, specifically expressing fears of being exposed as a fraud and potentially losing their current position. Observed behavior included anxious presentation and cognitive rehearsal of negative outcomes.

Intervention
Explored the client's worst-case narrative regarding the upcoming interview to identify cognitive distortions related to imposter syndrome. Facilitated an evidence-based examination for and against the thought 'I'm a fraud' to promote cognitive restructuring. Utilized Socratic questioning to challenge the assumption that not knowing every answer in meetings equates to being a fraud. Conducted a short mock interview targeting one difficult question to reduce performance anxiety and practice adaptive coping in session.

Response
Client actively engaged in identifying evidence against the belief of being a fraud, acknowledging positive performance reviews and prior promotions alongside isolated instances of not knowing meeting answers. Client demonstrated insight when prompted via Socratic questioning, recognizing that managers also do not possess every answer and that gaps in knowledge do not validate the 'fraud' narrative. Following the mock interview, the client reported that the experience was less distressing than anticipated.

Plan
Continue monitoring anxiety and preparation related to the upcoming team lead interview. Review outcomes of the interview and process any related cognitions in the next session. Assigned tasks were not discussed.
